message.content:
The sea usually looks **blue**—the same reason the sky does. Water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange) more strongly than shorter ones (blue, violet), so when sunlight hits it, the blue light is scattered back into our eyes. That’s why we see a deep blue ocean on clear days.

But the exact hue can vary:

| Condition | Typical Color |
|-----------|---------------|
| Clear, calm water | Deep blue |
| Shallow, sandy bottoms | Turquoise or greenish‑blue |
| Lots of algae or phytoplankton | Green or olive |
| Near shore with sediment | Brownish or muddy |
| Over ice or snow | White or pale blue |

So while “blue” is the classic answer, the sea can look anything from turquoise to green to brown depending on depth, clarity, and what’s floating in it.
